Finger-like projections extending into open water
Tooth-like symmetrical shape built by opposing waves
Formed at drowned river mouths filled with sediment

items: The Ganga-Brahmaputra Delta (Sundarbans) is an Arcuate Delta and the largest river delta globally.
West-flowing Indian rivers like Narmada and Tapti form estuaries instead of deltas due to rift valley topography and high flow speed.
The Mississippi River is a prime example of a Bird-foot Delta frequently asked in physical geography MCQs.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Depositional landforms by rivers are predominantly formed in the lower course where slope gradient decreases and river velocity slows down.
Deltas are wetlands created as rivers drop sediment load at their mouths upon entering a slower-moving body of water.
Arcuate deltas are fan-shaped landforms with a convex margin towards the sea, such as the Ganga and Nile deltas.
Bird-foot deltas have long, narrow distributary channels projecting into the sea, classic to the Mississippi River.
Cuspate deltas feature tooth-like shapes formed where river sediments are evenly shaped by strong sea waves.
Rivers flowing into deep seas with strong tides or through rocky terrains often form estuaries rather than deltas.
